Subject: Greenleaf Payments — inference discovery & ops plan

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap so we have a single place to iterate from and to make the upcoming technical deep-dive more focused. I kept this intentionally short; happy to expand on any bullet.

High-level goals you shared
- Replace the brittle rule-based scoring and offload fraud-suspect enrichment to an LLM-backed scoring service.
- Keep inference costs predictable while meeting auth-path latency targets.
- Maintain PCI scope and keep all cardholder data in your VPC (no tokenized payload leaving).

Pain points and constraints
- Tail latency variability: some auth flows spike and push median latency up and cause timeouts in the downstream service.
- Throughput profile: steady baseline for batch jobs and frequent short spikes (bursts) during peak hours.
- Compliance: SOC2 + PCI constraints; procurement expects documentation and a minimal on-prem footprint.

Preliminary SLO targets (for discussion in technical deep-dive)
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms for typical 128–256 token responses; p99 <= 350 ms as an aspirational target for same path.
- Bulk inference: ability to sustain 150–250 RPS steady state with bursts to ~600 RPS for short windows (30–120s).
- Availability: 99.9% platform availability for the dedicated inference tier.

Model and accuracy notes
- Primary model: handful of conversational/classification prompts and single-turn scoring; target model family: 7B–13B class (quantized 4/8-bit acceptable) — tradeoff: 13B tends to improve recall for nuanced fraud signals.
- Max sequence length: 1024 tokens should be sufficient; we heard you use ~200 tokens on average.

Recommended deployment topology (initial proposal)
1) Private VPC private-facing Redwood Private control plane + customer-managed data path.
2) Dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) for the auth path: pinned replicas with warm KV cache for low tail latency.
3) Autoscale policy for non-auth batch workers (shorter warm-up acceptable).
4) Fallback policy: if dedicated pool is saturated, route to a lighter quantized variant in the hosted tier (same interface) with throttling back to maintain latency.

Attachments I attached: Greenleaf_PoC_SOW_v0.1.pdf (draft scope & timelines), greenleaf-inference-sample-traffic.csv (your sample QPS distribution), SOC2-snapshot-2026.pdf (redwood SOC2 summary).

Next steps
- Please confirm the PoC target window (you mentioned ~6 weeks) and the procurement contacts.
- Rajiv: can you share the per-request payload size and whether you require full-card redaction before inference?
- We'll schedule a technical deep-dive with one of our runtime leads + infra specialist — propose Wed 2027-07-14 or Thu 2027-07-15.

Thanks — I’ll sync with Aditya on timing and circulate an updated SOW after your confirmation.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Thanks, Grace — this is perfect and more or less matches our notes. A couple clarifications from my side:

- Timeline: Procurement is targeting a 6–8 week PoC + evaluation window. We want an initial 4-week technical PoC and then a 2–4 week validation period with shadowed traffic.
- Data residency: All inference calls touching cardholder environments must remain in our us-east-1 VPC. We can provide a temporary service account for the PoC.
- Procurement: I’ve looped in procurement@greenleafpay.com — they will need a cost estimate and a redline-friendly contract skeleton (do not include open-data clauses).

We also noted the p95/p99 targets you proposed. For business-critical auth flows, anything >400 ms at p99 is not acceptable — those are usually our real-money flows. If you think 200/350 is achievable we should try to land there in the PoC, otherwise we need to scope the mitigation steps (circuit breakers, local cache).

Happy to take Wed 07/14 10:00am ET for the tech deep-dive. Rajiv, can you and your infra lead make it?

—Elena
Elena Park
Head of Product — Risk & Fraud | Greenleaf Payments
elena@greenleafpay.com

Subject: Re: Greenleaf Payments — inference discovery & ops plan

Thanks — quick tech notes from my side before the deep-dive. I pulled in the sample traffic (attached) and highlighted the following constraints: 

- Payload and tokenization: average payload ~180 tokens after normalization; worst-case 520 tokens for enrichment-heavy requests. We need to test with 512–1024 sequence windows.
- Memory constraints: our node preference is 80 GB GPU memory per replica (NVIDIA A40 / H100 class depending on availability). Can you confirm expected memory footprint for quantized 13B vs 7B for serving with a 1024 window? Also, what is the KV cache memory per request you observe?
- SLO realism: for auth path we need p95 <= 250 ms and p99 <= 500 ms for up to 512 tokens. If achieving 200/350 is feasible in the PoC we will celebrate, but please flag any tradeoffs (batching vs per-request latency, cache warm-up).
- Security: we will not allow outgoing data to third-party storage; introspection logs must be stored in our S3 under a restricted bucket.

Attached: greenleaf-inference-sample-traffic.csv (we exported the actual short-burst distribution).

Looking forward to the deep-dive — 07/14 10:00am ET works for us. Please include someone from your runtime team who can discuss kernel selection / quantization impacts and an infra contact for VPC peering and KMS integration.

Rajiv Singh
CTO | Greenleaf Payments
rajiv@greenleafpay.com

Summary
- Account: Greenleaf Payments (Fintech, PCI scope).
- PoC window: target 6 weeks (4-week tech PoC, 2-week validation).
- Key SLO asks: p95 target ~200–250ms; p99 target <= 500ms for up to 512 tokens; baseline 150–250 RPS with spikes to ~600 RPS.
- Topology request: Private VPC + Dedicated GPU pool + fallback hosted variant.

Action items
- Aditya: prepare an updated SOW with PoC milestones, success criteria (latency thresholds, accuracy thresholds, shadow run plan) and estimated committed capacity cost. Include an option for dedicated reserved pool vs hybrid burst to hosted. Due EOD Wed 07/14. (aditya_rao@redwood.ai)
- Monica: own the technical PoC success criteria document and coordinate runtime lead. Please prepare a checklist (dataset ingestion, sequence-length tests, KV cache warming tests, p95/p99 measurement plan). Due COB Thu 07/15. (monica_patel@redwood.ai)
- Grace: schedule the Wed 07/14 10:00am ET deep-dive with runtime + infra. Invite list: runtime_lead@redwood.ai, infra_ops@redwood.ai, aditya_rao, monica_patel. I will attach the draft SOW and the sample traffic to the calendar invite.

Notes for the deep-dive
- Bring quantization memory/latency estimates for 7B/13B at 4/8-bit and expected KV cache sizes.
- Prepare a brief on fallback routing (policy examples) and how we maintain transparent billing during fallbacks.

I’ll follow up once Aditya posts the SOW.

Thanks —
